detail:
fnn-bpo-call-with-owner-journal (bp-obligation.lisp:34) installs a private owner (fnn-owner-install, owner.lisp:1565) and runs its thunk in fnn-quantum-command (bp-obligation.lisp:44, section def at owner.lisp:2730 -> O). Thunks reach: fnn-carry-execute (bp-obligation.lisp:350-351 write-sequence, finish-output on *fnn-stdout*), and fnn-bpo-request-publish (bp-obligation.lisp:178) -> fnn-bpo-request-pause (bp-obligation.lisp:142-143: fnn-out, finish-output, then (loop (sleep 1)) -- a process-death witness gated by fnn-developer-selector, a developer image only).
Keys: R2|fnn-carry-execute|O:write-sequence, R2|fnn-carry-execute|O:finish-output, R2|fnn-bpo-request-pause|O:finish-output, R2|fnn-bpo-request-pause|O:sleep.
Hazard: O is provably held; but the owner is private to a one-shot command process (the store is opened exclusively: 'a served store refuses (already locked)', bp-obligation.lisp:~329; no serving threads were found in the head of fnn-owner-install), so no other section contends. The sleep is intentional and developer-image-only. Not verified: that fnn-owner-install starts no thread at all beyond its first ~45 lines.
fix: Justify by a design decision: declare these one-shot command sites as R2 exceptions (private owner, no contender; pause is a developer-image death witness), or move the report print outside the quantum (return the octets). Low priority.
notes: 10-06 21:41 PROVED, not moved: contract private_owner_commands (tools/lock_discipline_contracts.json) is verified by tools/lock_discipline_check.py verify_private_owner_commands. Owner constructed only by fnn-owner-install in the let of fnn-bpo-call-with-owner-journal; flow scan finds no store/publish/thread/actor start (one custody publication, fnn-owner-retain-run-authority, only on a failed open); commands reached only from the two registered one-shot dispatches. Exempts write-sequence/finish-output/sleep leaves in the runner+6 commands. Keys gone: R2 fnn-emit O:write-sequence/finish-output (weight 11, all bpo), fnn-carry-execute O:{write-sequence,finish-output}, fnn-bpo-request-pause O:{finish-output,sleep}. Side effects: fnn-extent-read-stall O:sleep 145->130 (still new); fnn-emit baseline rows (count 3) now stale for the integrator to lower; LOCK-R2-LISTENER-RECONFIG-STDOUT quotes the fnn-emit keys, which now vanish as it anticipated. Diff in /tmp/lpo-gate.txt. Markers still printed under O: intact.
scenario: Offline `fn operator ... carry list/inspect' with a blocked stdout holds a private owner mutex; no other thread waits. The pause only fires with FN_BP_OBLIGATION_TEST_PAUSE_AFTER_ATTEMPT on a developer image.
